exclusion_detail: Both reactants of lead 5b were inferred from the product name and a mechanism sentence, not read in the paper; the pyridazine reactant 1a is probably not purchasable. (Reclassified 2026-10-24 from the reader's route.)

lead.label: 5b
lead.why: Only phthalazine (5b) showed broad spectrum anti-tumor activity ... (5b) exhibited the highest growth inhibitory activity against CNS-SNB-75 cell line ... Phthalazine (5b) may be an effective, convenient and safe anti-cancer agent

reactions.conditions: General procedure 4.1.1: equimolar (0.01 mol) 1a and 2b in EtOH (30 mL) with catalytic piperidine (1.0 mL), microwave labStation, 70 C, 5 min; solid filtered and crystallised from dioxane; yield 85%
reactions.source: Main article Section 2.1 (Scheme 1 text) and Section 4.1.1 (general procedure and 5b characterisation); no SI file

notes: The text layer has no structures, so BOTH reactant structures are inferred, not read: 1a = ethyl 1-aryl-5-cyano-1,6-dihydro-4-methyl-6-oxo-3-pyridazinecarboxylate with aryl = phenyl (5a-c carry N3-phenyl; 5d,e use 1b with tolyl); 2b = 2-(thiophen-2-ylmethylene)malononitrile (the paper calls 2a-e 'arylidinemalononitriles' in Section 2 but 'cinnamonitrile derivatives' in the abstract/experimental). Support: the mechanism text says aromatisation 'by elimination of HCN', and atom balance 1a (C15H13N3O3) + 2b (C8H4N2S) = 5b (C22H16N4O3S) + HCN is exact; a 3-(thienyl)acrylonitrile would not balance without loss of H2. Neither reactant has a name, source or preparation in the paper (experimental says chemicals from Aldrich and Merck, but 1a is a bespoke pyridazine from the authors' earlier work, refs 50-55, and is probably not purchasable); I marked both 'commercial' only because the paper uses them without describing any preparation. The printed product name omits the locant '1-' of the carboxylate, so OPSIN may fail on it; the intended compound is the 1-carboxylate (C1 of the phthalazine, from the pyridazine C3 ester).
